result.topic_en: Orbit determination: setting up auxiliary angles from the node and inclination, and expressing the squared distance kk between two heliocentric positions of a body in terms of the distances ρ, ρ' and the Earth's (Sun's) coordinates, including the special case of ecliptic reference with B = B' = 0; a numeric table runs along the right margin.
result.transcription:
184 Mo[?]
Nio[?] nath.[?]
Litt. R.

1) Man mache
$\tan b = \tan i \sin(\alpha - N)$ \quad $\frac{\tan(\alpha-N)}{\cos i} = \tan\lambda$
$\tan b' = \tan i \sin(\alpha' - N)$ \quad $\frac{\tan(\alpha'-N)}{\cos i} = \tan\lambda'$

2) Man mache A auf $\odot$ Ort lich[?] bezeichnet[?]
$R\cos(A-N) - R'\cos(A'-N) = p\cos\psi\cos(i-\varphi)$
$R\sin(A-N) - R'\sin(A'-N) = p\sin\psi\cos\varphi$
$R\tan B - R'\tan B' = p\sin\psi\sin\varphi$
Und man wird haben
$kk = \left(\varrho - \frac{p\sin(\lambda'-\psi)\cos(i-\varphi)}{\sin(\lambda'-\lambda)}\right)^2 + \left(\varrho' - \frac{p\sin(\lambda-\psi)\cos(i-\varphi)}{\sin(\lambda'-\lambda)}\right)^2 - 2\,\mathrm{prod.} \times \cos(\lambda'-\lambda)$
$+ (p\sin\psi\sin i-\varphi)^2$
$= \cos\tfrac12(\lambda'-\lambda)^2 \left\{\varrho' - \varrho + \frac{p\cos(\frac12(\lambda+\lambda')-\psi)\cos(i-\varphi)}{\cos\frac12(\lambda'-\lambda)}\right\}^2$
$+ \sin\tfrac12(\lambda'-\lambda)^2 \left\{\varrho' + \varrho - \frac{p\sin(\frac12\lambda+\frac12\lambda'-\psi)\cos(i-\varphi)}{\sin\frac12(\lambda'-\lambda)}\right\}^2$
$+ (p\sin\psi\sin(i-\varphi))^2$
Wenn man die Ekliptik zum Grunde legt und $B, B' = 0$ setzt so hat man statt 2
$R\cos(A-N) - R'\cos(A'-N) = D\cos\psi$
$\cos i(R\sin(A-N) - R'\sin(A'-N)) = D\sin\psi$
$kk = \cos\tfrac12(\lambda'-\lambda)^2\left\{\varrho'-\varrho + \frac{D\cos(\psi-\frac12\lambda-\frac12\lambda')}{\cos\frac12(\lambda'-\lambda)}\right\}^2 + \sin\tfrac12(\lambda'-\lambda)^2\left\{\varrho'+\varrho + \frac{D\sin(\psi-\frac12\lambda-\frac12\lambda')}{\sin\frac12(\lambda'-\lambda)}\right\}^2$
$+ (D\sin\psi\tan i)^2$
oder wenn man $\varrho' = \mu\varrho$ setzt,
mache man $(1-\mu)\cos\tfrac12(\lambda'-\lambda) = t\cos\theta$
$(1+\mu)\sin\tfrac12(\lambda'-\lambda) = t\sin\theta$
$-D\cos(\theta+\psi-\tfrac12\lambda-\tfrac12\lambda') = et$
$D\,(\sin(\theta+\psi-\tfrac12\lambda-\tfrac12\lambda')^2 + \sin\psi^2\tan i^2) = f$ \quad und es wird seyn
$kk =$ [-$tt\varrho+e$-] $tt(\varrho+e)^2 + ff$

methods.what: Auxiliary angles: latitude b and argument λ from right-ascension-like angle α, node N and inclination i
Reduction of the difference of two solar position vectors to polar auxiliary quantities p, ψ, φ
Squared distance kk between two positions expressed as sum of squares in half-sum/half-difference angles
Special case with ecliptic as reference plane (B=B'=0): simplified auxiliary D, ψ and formula for kk
With ρ'=μρ, introduce t, θ, e, f so that kk is a quadratic in ρ of form t²(ρ+e)²+f²
Numerical table of values for arguments 0.000–0.037
